chunks: 13 – Sulayman ibn Ya'qub, al-Nakha'i. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated to me, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Durustawayh narrated to me, he said: Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said:
Sulayman ibn Ya'qub al-Nakha'i used to lie upon the waqf (prophetic/imam's narration).

key_terms.الْوَقْفُ: The state of stopping or attributing a narration to a specific source (like an Imam) without a continuous chain; often used to mean 'attributing falsely' in this context.
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ: A prominent Shia narrator known for his extensive narrations, here critiqued for a specific flaw.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a narrator is said to 'lie upon the waqf'?
ai.summary: This biographical note from 'Ilal al-Sharayid (or similar rijal text) states that Sulayman ibn Ya'qub al-Nakha'i was known to 'lie upon the waqf,' a technical term in hadith sciences meaning he would attribute narrations to the Imams (or the Prophet) that were not actually from them, either by mistake or deliberately.

en.tashayyu: 13 – Sulaymān b. Yaʿqūb, al-Nakhaʿī.  Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Muḥammad b. al-Faḍl narrated to me, he said: ʿAbdullāh b. Jaʿfar b. Durustawayh narrated to me, he said: Yaʿqūb b. Sufyān said:
Sulaymān b. Yaʿqūb al-Nakhaʿī used to keep to (? lie upon) the waqf.
